data.demo_plan_content:
# Projects space

## Intent
Give a clear view of how each project is moving.

## Scopes
1. Atlas — navigation, structure and interactions.
2. Nova — components, empty states and filters.
3. Echo — journey validation and accessibility.

## Success criteria
- Find a project in fewer than three interactions.
- Tell active projects from archives.
- Share the context without rereading a conversation.

This document belongs to the sample wish.

demo.report_content:
# Example wish report

The decisions were applied to the scoping artifact. The three scopes went through their states: waiting, working, decision and done.

This report describes a simulation of the interface. No project code, paid model or external test was run.

## Your next step
Annotate the artifact in Review, then approve the move to delivery.

demo_supports.guide_content:
# A demo to play with

All the contributions and data of this wish are **simulated**. No model or external service is called.

| Capability | Where to try it |
| --- | --- |
| Charts, table, mini-app | Interactive lab: volume, line chart, search, statuses |
| Markdown graph | Mermaid graph: source and enlargement |
| Editable diagram | The wish at a glance: editing the nodes |
| Journey mockup | Projects space: layout choice |
| GFM document | This guide: table, checklist, read/edit/preview |
| Code | Visual answer contract: viewable source |
| Screenshot | Graphic preview: embedded image |
| Blocking decision | Answer Q01, then start the demo |
| Contributions | Agents and timeline: explicit simulated overlap |
| Review | Add feedback on an artifact and resolve it |
| Source of truth | Mark an artifact and keep its human revision |
| Session | Export the wish, then import its copy |

## Real limits
The lab's internal settings are temporary. The HTML source, the artifacts, decisions and revisions are saved in the session. System notifications and real providers are checked separately in an installed app; the demo does not claim to have validated them.

## To explore
- [ ] Change the volume and switch to the line chart
- [ ] Filter the table and move a card forward
- [ ] Enlarge the Mermaid diagram
- [ ] Edit a document, then find its revision
- [ ] Export the session

Reference for the concept of visual answers: [T3 Code, PR #15968](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/pull/15968). This demo is an original work for Djinn's isolated engine.
demo_supports.headline: An answer can become a small application
demo_supports.intro: Djinn demo · all the data is fictional. Charts, filters and interactions work locally. Body text and controls: 12 px.
demo_supports.mermaid_content:
# A graph right in the Markdown

Simulated example: design and build have independent scopes. The verification uses both of their results.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  M[Wish] --> D[Design]
  M --> C[Build]
  D --> V[Verification]
  C --> V
  V --> H[Human approval]
```

The diagram is rendered locally, with no CDN. Show its source or enlarge it. The editable JSON diagram stays available in the “The wish at a glance” artifact.
